There's a big difference between Digg and Reddit: money.

Digg was, as far as companies go, tiny. In spite of Reddit trying to frequently play the "small guy who somehow made it big $4 of gold at a time" card, they're anything but. Conde Naste owns Reddit (source being a Conde Naste job description). Conde Naste also owns Ars Technica, GQ, Vogue, Wired, Epicurious, and a whole lot more. Conde Naste in turn is owned by Advance Publications. Advance Publications owns literally dozens of major newspapers and websites, numerous television channels, magazines, and so on. Advance Publications has revenue of around $8,000,000,000 per year .

Reddit's going downhill fast, but I can't even try to intelligently speculate about what that's going to mean in the long run.
